weapons.about: The carrier's guns, her point defence and her torpedoes, and the raider that attacks her (src/carrier/weapons.mjs). There are no shields: what keeps a ship alive is armour (`integrity.armour`), point defence, and not being where the shot is aimed. `turrets`: each heavy turret is a `mount` (its id, also the name of its gunhouse in hull.glb, and `<id>-guns` its barrels), fed from its `magazine` compartment up its `barbette`; `from` is the hatch you man it from (deck, spot, the way you face when you leave). `gun`, for every turret: `shell` muzzle speed m/s, `reload` seconds per barrel, `crewReload` the same for a turret its crew fires, `train` and `elevate` the fastest it turns (degrees a second), `elevation` its limits (degrees, toward the side the turret stands on), `rack` rounds in the ready rack, `stock` rounds in the magazine, `hoist` seconds to send one round up, `spread` the aim error of a shot (radians), `crewSpread` how far off a crew lays the guns, `range` metres a shell flies, `damage` what one does to the raider's hull, `fouled` metres of line of fire checked against the hull, `heat` what one shot puts into the ship's heat sinks (0 to 1 of them). `pdc`: the point defence cannons, rotary guns on the layout's `pdc` mounts, run by the fire-control computer: each one takes the nearest torpedo (or, with none, the raider inside `raiderRange`) that is within `range` and `arc` degrees of where the mount faces, leads it (for its acceleration too), slews at `slew` degrees a second and fires `rate` tracers a second (each tracer stands for a burst of rounds) at `speed` m/s, off by `spread` radians; a tracer passing within `radius` metres of a torpedo kills it, and one that meets the raider does `damage`. `stock` is the tracers each mount's magazine holds (its `magazine` in the mounts), `heat` what each tracer puts into the sinks. A mount is as healthy as the compartment it is fixed to. `torpedo`: every torpedo, either side's: `accel` m/s² for `burn` seconds, launched at `push` m/s, gone after `life` seconds; `jink` m/s² of random weave once it is within `terminal` metres (what makes point defence miss); `fuse` metres from its target it goes off. Into the carrier it does `pen`, `damage` and `hole` as a shell does (integrity.mjs), never stopped by the armour; into the raider, `raiderDamage`. `tubes`: the carrier's own torpedo tubes, fired by the CIC at a raider between `range` metres: `salvo` at a time, `every` seconds, from `magazine` while it holds `stock`, out of the hull at `at` (ship frame) along `dir`. `raider`: its `hull` (armour and all), `speed` (m/s past the carrier) and `accel`, `jink` (m/s² of evasive weave, changing every second or two: what makes a long shot miss), `standoff` (the range of its passes, metres), `passes`, `size` (half-axes of the ellipsoid shells hit), its `gun` (`shell` m/s, seconds `every` between shots, `spread`, `range`), its `torpedo` launches (a `salvo` every `every` seconds while the carrier is between `range` metres, `stock` in all), its own point defence `pdc` against the carrier's torpedoes (`range`, `rate`, `spread`, `speed`), and its `flak` at a fighter within `range`: a shot `every` so many seconds at `shell` m/s, aimed where she will be if she flies on as she is, off by up to `spread` radians, doing `damage` if it passes within `radius` metres of her. `target`: the gunnery drill's sled, towed `tow` metres astern of a tug on `passes` straight passes `standoff` metres off at `speed`; `size` is the ellipsoid a shell must pass through to score, `clear` how far off the tug is gone. It has no hull to lose: hits are counted. `fighter`: the fighter's twin cannon: `shell` m/s on top of her own velocity, seconds `every` between rounds, `spread`, `range` metres a round flies, `rounds` in the drum (refilled on the pad), the `damage` one round does to a raider (or a torpedo, within `radius`), and her own `hull` (mended on the pad; at nothing she is dead in space and flight control brings her in). `railgun`: the broadside railguns (their own `about`). `broadside`: the torpedo broadside (its own `about`).

from.label: Up the hoist trunk to the bow dorsal turret
Down to the bow ventral turret
Up to the stern dorsal turret
Down to the stern ventral turret

gun.calibreNote: 14 m barrels; muzzle speed 5300 m/s in the design (the game's gun.shell is still tuned for play).

railgun.about: Two fixed railguns, one a side, firing out of the hangar walls along the beam: `port` and `starboard` each have a `muzzle` (ship frame), the `dir` it fires and the `room` it stands in (below 20% health it cannot fire). Each has its own capacitors (`charge` seconds to fill, on main power only) and `stock` slugs. A slug of `slug` kg leaves at `speed` m/s on top of her velocity, off by `spread`; it does `damage` to the raider and is gone after `range` m; each shot puts `heat` into the sinks, and its kick pushes the ship (weapons.mjs `recoil`). The guns cannot train: the helm turns her (and rolls her) until the line of one side runs through where the raider will be, and fires (Q). A side bears when its slug would pass inside `window` of the raider's hit ellipsoid (1 is its skin); with nobody at the helm the CIC fires a side that bears, which a raider passing above or below her beam never does.

bandit.about: The raider's escort fighters (weapons/bandits.mjs): Rook fighters flown on the same `Flight` as yours (the layout's `fighter`: mass, thrust, tanks, jets) by an AI pilot. `count` come with each raid, in `slots` (metres in the raider's frame; a third and fourth go twice as far out). `hull` (the cannon does `fighter.damage` a round) and the hit ellipsoid `size` about `centre`. Once the raider is on its firing passes and the carrier is inside `start` m they strafe her point defence: runs along her side `pass` m out, at `run` m/s past her (closing on the line at up to `close` m/s, `gain` per metre off it), each started `fire` + `lead` m short of the gun, firing from `fire` m, turning for the next `extend` m past the gun; `look` s ahead they keep `clearance` m off her hull. The nearest to your fighter inside `engage` m (and any you have hit) fights you, holding at about `stand` m. With a target in reach it only turns away to burn when its velocity is `shootSlack` m/s off what it wants; less than that its side jets take out. `bingo` (a fraction of either tank, the drive's or the jets') sends one back to the raider; at `clear` m from the carrier, leaving, it is gone. `jink`: inside `near` m of the carrier or your fighter, a `pop` s random pop on the side jets every `every` s (the jets' tank is small: held, they would empty it in a minute). Shooting, the side jets take out more than `trim` m/s of the velocity it wants across the nose. `gun`: rounds at `shell` m/s on top of its own velocity, one every `every` s in bursts of `burst` s with `pause` s between, `spread` per round and `err` (radians) per burst, gone after `range` m; a round within `radius` m of your fighter does `damage`, within `pdcRadius` m of a point defence gun takes `pdcDamage` off its 100, and through a spread radiator hurts it by `radiator`; the nose must be within `cone` radians of the lead to fire. `missiles`: heat-seekers it carries (the layout's `missile`), the first not before `missileFirst` s into its fight, then one every `missileEvery` s at most, fired at your fighter when the seeker on its nose has locked her inside `missileRange` m.

heat.about: How bright each thing is in the infrared, for the heat-seekers (weapons/missiles.mjs heatSources). A fighter (yours or a bandit): `base`, plus `drive` × its main drive's power, plus `jets` while any side jet fires. The raider: `base`, plus `drive` while it burns on its passes. The carrier: `base`, plus `radiators` × how far her radiators are spread × (0.3 + the heat in her sinks), plus `drive` × her push. A torpedo while its motor burns: `torpedo`. A seeker sees I / r², r in km.

missile.about: The fighters' heat-seeking missiles (weapons/missiles.mjs). `rails` on each fighter, yours reloaded on the pad. On the rail the seeker looks along the nose, or at the selected contact when it is within `offBore` radians of the nose, and locks the brightest thing in a `gate`-radian cone above `sense` (I / r², r in km). Fired (Q), it leaves at `push` m/s down off the rail, lights after `drop` s and burns at `accel` m/s² for `burn` s, steering by proportional navigation; then its divert jets turn it at up to `divert` m/s² until `divertDv` m/s is spent. In flight the seeker keeps to its `gate` round what it tracks, which counts `hold` times as bright as it is; with nothing in the gate it looks over `fov` radians. Each flare it takes for the brightest thing in view it judges once: `reject` of the time it sees it for a flare and looks past it from then on. Armed after `arm` s, it goes off within `fuse` m of anything hot but its launcher (a flare too), and is gone after `life` s. A point defence round (the carrier's or the raider's) that passes within `hitBy` m of it shoots it down. It does `damage` to a fighter, `ship` × that to the raider, and on the carrier hits like a shell of `carrier.pen` armour, `carrier.damage` to the room and `carrier.hole` to its hull.

flares.about: Flares, on every ship (weapons/missiles.mjs). Each is thrown out at `eject` m/s on top of the ship's velocity and burns for `life` s at its kind's `heat`, fading. Your fighter drops `fighter.salvo` a press of G, from `fighter.count`, refilled on the pad. The AI ships (`bandit`, `raider`, `carrier`) flare when a missile tracking them is inside `react` m, after `notice` s to see it: `salvo` at a time, one salvo every `every` s, while their `count` lasts; a bandit also cuts its drive for `coast` s.

brace.about: Brace for impact. When one of the raider's torpedoes will arrive within `eta` seconds the ship calls brace and counts down (weapons/torpedoes.mjs braceFrame), and the brace straps on the weightless rooms' walls show "Strap in"; the countdown stays up `hold` s after the last one. A hit kicks the structure: `kick` m/s at the hit for a torpedo (`shell` for a gun shell, `glance` for one the armour stopped), less with distance (`fade` m halves it). Strapped in, you ride it; a hand on a rail holds below `grip` m/s and your feet in a rail below `feet` m/s; anyone else keeps going. Meeting a wall faster than `hurt` m/s hurts, `per` of an injury for each m/s over; a whole one (1) blacks you out (the damage control party picks you up), and it heals at `heal` a minute.

broadside.about: The hangar walls' torpedo tubes, launched cold sideways: `per` a side, each side fed from its two ordnance rooms (a side whose magazines are both below 20% health cannot fire). `stock` torpedoes a side; `salvo` per firing; `reload` seconds between a side's salvos; `first` seconds into a raid before the first (the CIC's solution); `arc` degrees off the beam the raider must be within, and `range` [min, max] m; `push` m/s out of the tube and `cold` seconds before the motor lights. The CIC fires the side that bears; with you at the helm, a click does.
